nina: Heads-up: onboarding Nova-7B int4 hit a weird drift when running longform summarization. After ~1500 tokens the model starts repeating paraphrases and confidence distribution tightens.

paul: repro details? tokenizer, seq, sampling?

nina: Nova7B_bf16 -> Nova7B_int4 (our quant). Tokenizer: merged-unicode-bpe (we unioned bpe and legacy spm). Seq=2048, temp=0.2 nucleus=0.9, batch=1.

harry: did you compare pre/post rotary tables? Mixed head dims can cause interp mismatch if conversion uses different cos/sin packing.

ci-bot: quick-eval queued: run_eval --model nova7b_int4 --task longform --seq 2048 --seed 7

ci-bot: quick result: repetition onset ~1532 tokens, top tokens cycle among 5-7 common words.

sala: dump token ids around onset?

nina: token ids window 1528..1536: [512, 1990, 512, 1990, 512, 1990, 88, 44] -> clear 2-id motif.

paul: tokenizer union might have deduped different codepoint sequences into same id (e.g., precomposed vs decomposed accents). That creates small attractors. Also check our rotary interpolation: we downsampled cos/sin table and used linear interp in quant build. That interpolation error can accumulate over many steps.

harry: two quick experiments: A) keep rotary table full precision (bf16) and disable table downsample/interp; B) run with tokenizer remap disabled (use original ids).

ci-bot: runs started.

ci-bot: Run A done: repetition eliminated in 10/10 quick runs, latency +4.6%.

ci-bot: Run B done: repetition delayed but still occurs in 6/10 runs. Token stream shows fewer exact repeats.

sala: seems numeric error in rotary accumulation is primary. Token aliasing amplifies. Proposal: change conversion tooling to avoid downsampling cos/sin (store compressed bf16) and add a validator that asserts no token id collisions for unicode canonically-equivalent sequences.

paul: opened PR #4902 to adjust conversion and add longform regression (seq=4096) to nightly. Also drafting onboarding note: Nova-7B-int4 will retain rotary tables in bf16 for now.

nina: I'll follow up on tokenizer union audit. harry: can you run perf impact analysis for bf16 rotary?

harry: on it. tagging infra for nightly job. cc @product for advisory mention. :thumbsup:
